text:
ashley: Quick design q: should we switch from a single-file activation marker to a two-step prepare+commit for air-gapped upgrades? Thinking about powercut and auditability.

jonah: Two-step seems safer. Prepare unpacks + validates, writes a `prepare.json` with operator id + manifest hash. Commit flips an immutable pointer. That gives us a clear window to run smoke tests.

maria: +1. Also helps with audit logs: we can attach operator-signed attestations to the prepare artifact. If commit fails mid-rename, activator can consult prepare.json to resume or roll back.

leo: Concern: more on-disk objects ==> more GC complexity. We should garbage collect old prepares after commit or ttl. Also need to avoid races when multiple prepares arrive for same model id. Maybe use content-hash + monotonic nonce for dir name.

ashley: Proposed sequence:
1) artifact-bot deposits tarball -> verifier extracts to /opt/redwood/prepares/<model>-<hash>-<nonce>/
2) verifier writes `prepare.json` (fields: manifest_hash, sig, operator, timestamp)
3) operator runs offline smoke runner against prepare dir -> writes `smoke.result` (pass/fail + logs)
4) operator issues `commit` via admin socket (signed request) -> activator checks prepare.sig + smoke.result and creates `active/<model>-<hash>/` by creating an atomic symlink `active/current-<model>` -> fsync dir -> write audit record `activations.log`
5) GC clears stale prepare dirs older than X days if not committed

jonah: Force-commit option for emergencies? Maybe require higher-level approval or a flag `--force-unverified` that records explicit justification in audit log.

maria: We must enforce offline-only smoke: no calls to external telemetry or model zoo. Ship a small harness binary with each package that performs in-memory load and one inference. Keep harness hermetic.

leo: Rollback strategy: keep `active/previous-<model>-<hash>/` symlink for N last activations. Activator should keep last two active images locally. On commit, copy pointer `active/previous` <- `active/current` before switching to new. That gives O(1) rollback. Note: copying pointers not files.

ashley: How do we handle partial commit if process dies while switching symlink? Use atomic rename of symlink file: write `active/tmp-<rand>` then rename to `active/current-<model>`. Filesystems usually make rename atomic. Also fsync parent dir after rename.

artifact-bot: artifact-bot: upload complete 1720600123 -> model:redwood-alg-1 hash:abc123 nonce:5 staged at prepares/redwood-alg-1-abc123-5

jonah: Metrics gating: commit should optionally delay final cutover until local resource checks pass (disk, GPU memory). If checks fail post-commit, activator should revert to previous automatically and raise alert. That implies commit has two phases: symlink switch + post-check verification. If post-check fails, revert.

maria: For lease/ownership: binds prepare to operator session id + expiry. If operator loses session, activator reclaims prepare after short TTL and marks prepare as orphaned. Orphans can be revalidated by support with attached smoke logs.

leo: Testing: add chaos tests: kill activator during rename, simulate disk-full during commit, and delayed fsync behavior on slow filesystem. Add unit test for audit log consistency.

ashley: Ops runbook bullets: how to force-commit with signed justification, how to triage orphaned prepares, how to manually recreate symlink pointer in worst-case, and where to find smoke.runner logs. Keep steps minimal.

maria: RFC follow-up: I'll sketch prepare+commit proto, include sample `prepare.json` schema and audit log format. Will include CLI examples for `redwoodctl prepare` and `redwoodctl commit --sign`.

jonah: One more UX note: per-customer config to disable auto-GC or keep longer history for compliance customers. Defaults should be conservative (short TTL).

ashley: Great. I'll write the runbook appendix and schedule a quick sync with security for the attestation signing requirements. Thanks everyone :heart:
